notices.text: GCAM Studio is the engineering viewer of a Monte Carlo simulator. Every count, image, spectrum and waveform it shows is simulated; it is not a measuring instrument, and nothing it shows is a measurement of a real source.

The four-output physical readout is an experimental simulation. Its calibration lines are offered or refused from a pinned record; a module that matches no preset is calibrated locally and is unvalidated; positioning deposits at other energies with a source-line calibration is a declared approximation whose accuracy is unvalidated.

Live time advances at the chosen speed (live seconds per wall second) and Stop acts when it is clicked, so the counts kept at a Stop differ from run to run even with a fixed seed. A fixed seed reproduces the acquisition itself.
Studio saves nothing on its own and keeps no settings: the scene, the results and the measurements live in memory and are gone when the window closes.
